Message from Alen Customer Experience Team:
Yes — I can help you choose confidently. 
When selecting the best air purifier, the two main factors to evaluate are: 
Room size (square footage): measure the room and compare it to the listed coverage area of the unit.
Your air quality concern: for example odors, allergies, smoke, mold, dust, pet dander, or asthma. As a general rule, HEPA filters provide the most thorough particle filtration, while carbon filters are better for odors or chemicals.
If your room is larger than a unit’s listed coverage area, it can still clean the room, but the rate of cleaning decreases. 
If you’re trying to cover multiple rooms (like a living room and bedroom), air purifiers work best in the room they’re placed in since they can’t work through walls or doorways. Two smaller units (one per room) is best; if you can only get one, place it in the room where you spend the most time (often the bedroom).

turns.q: How do I use it correctly to get the best result?
turns.replyTail: - Use the right speed for your space: - The maximum coverage rating applies on the highest speed. - Lower speeds will take longer to clean the room. - For multiple rooms, you may need more than one purifier since one unit can’t effectively move air through hallways and back. - If it’s your first purifier, the best place to start is the bedroom. - Next best spots are high-traffic areas like the living room or kitchen, especially if those areas are sources of irritants (like cooking or pet odors).
